posts.title: Whisking a softer matcha
posts.excerpt: Water just off the boil makes matcha bitter. Here is how we cool it, and why the whisk moves in an M.
posts.content:
Pour the boiled water into an empty bowl first, then into the tea bowl. Two pours take it down to about 80 degrees.

Whisk from the wrist in a quick M, not in circles, until fine foam covers the surface. Lift the whisk from the centre.

posts.title: The last bellflowers by the window
posts.excerpt: The bellflowers along the stepping stones are almost over. Come this week if you want to see them.
posts.content:
The first owner planted forty bellflowers along the path in 1974. About thirty still come back every summer.

When the last one closes, the maple by the veranda takes over, and our nerikiri turns red with it.

posts.title: Chestnut kinton is coming
posts.excerpt: From 1 November, chestnut kinton joins the tray. Boxes of six can be ordered three days ahead.
posts.content:
We steam the chestnuts, sieve them by hand and sweeten them only a little, so they still taste of the tree.

Kinton keeps for one day only. We make about sixty each morning, so ask us to keep some for you.
